description: Phase 6bh gate — UPSERT: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(col) DO UPDATE SET / DO NOTHING. Successor to OR REPLACE/IGNORE with explicit conflict target and update expression.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 999) ON CONFLICT(id) DO NOTHING;
SELECT id, v FROM t;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 999) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET v = 888;
SELECT id, v FROM t;

cases.name: upsert-do-update-set-excluded
cases.description: The special `excluded` table refers to the would-be-inserted row.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 999) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET v = excluded.v;
SELECT id, v FROM t;

cases.name: upsert-do-update-set-expr-old-plus-new
cases.description: UPDATE SET can reference both existing and excluded values.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 5) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET v = v + excluded.v;
SELECT id, v FROM t;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET v = 999;
SELECT id, v FROM t;

cases.name: upsert-where-clause-on-update
cases.description: UPDATE branch can have its own WHERE that filters whether the update fires.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 5) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET v = excluded.v WHERE v > 100;
SELECT id, v FROM t;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT, cnt INTEGER);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email ON t (email);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a@x', 1);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'a@x', 1) ON CONFLICT(email) DO UPDATE SET cnt = cnt + 1;
SELECT id, email, cnt FROM t ORDER BY id;

cases.name: upsert-conflict-target-missing-index
cases.description: ON CONFLICT(col) where col isn't a PK or unique-indexed column → COMPILE_NO_CONFLICT_TARGET.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10) ON CONFLICT(a) DO NOTHING;
